title: Bodh Gaya, Rajgir & Nalanda
selection: Bihar recorded 0.737 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, up 35% on 2023 (India Tourism Data Compendium 2025, Table 4.1.2). Bodh Gaya's Mahabodhi Temple and the Nalanda Mahavihara are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, and Nalanda's excavated site was the eighth most visited ticketed ASI monument for foreign visitors in FY 2024-25 (88,151).

images.caption: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya

overview.text:
Bodh Gaya is where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment, under the Bodhi tree beside what is now the Mahabodhi Temple — a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002 and the holiest place in the Buddhist world. Pilgrims come from across Asia and beyond, and Buddhist communities from Tibet, Japan, Thailand, Bhutan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and many other countries have built temples and monasteries in their own national styles around the town.

Days here are slow and contemplative: early mornings at the Mahabodhi complex among monks and pilgrims, visits to the monasteries, and the 80-foot Great Buddha statue consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 1989. Gaya airport is about 7 km away, and Gaya Junction station about 15 km. Rajgir and Nalanda, further north, complete Bihar's Buddhist circuit.

best_time.text: Bihar Tourism recommends September to April. Summers in Bihar are hot and winters cold — bring warm layers for early mornings in December and January.

how_to_reach.text: Gaya airport is about 7 km from Bodh Gaya, and Gaya Junction railway station about 15 km. Gaya itself is about 100 km south of Patna. Roads connect Bodh Gaya with Patna and other cities in Bihar.

local_transport.text: Auto-rickshaws and cycle-rickshaws are the easiest way to get around Bodh Gaya; the town centre around the Mahabodhi Temple is walkable.

overview.text:
The Mahabodhi Temple marks the place where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment. Emperor Ashoka is said to have built a stupa here in the 3rd century BCE, and the temple complex became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002.

The 4.8-hectare complex holds the main temple and, behind it, the Bodhi tree, believed to descend from the tree under which the Buddha sat. Around them are other sites linked to the weeks after his enlightenment, such as the Lotus Pond and the Animesh Lochan Chaitya. Monks and pilgrims meditate and chant throughout the day; the complex is especially busy at Buddha Jayanti in May or June and during the Nyingma Monlam Chenmo prayers each February.

items.title: Etiquette
items.body: Dress modestly, remove footwear and keep silent.

overview.text:
Rajgir, ringed by low hills, was the capital of the Magadha kings Bimbisara and Ajatashatru, contemporaries of the Buddha. The Buddha often stayed here, and Gridhakuta — Vulture Peak — is where he is said to have preached, including the Lotus Sermon. Rajgir is also sacred to Jains and Hindus.

A ropeway climbs Ratnagiri hill to the white Vishwa Shanti Stupa, the Peace Pagoda, with its four golden Buddhas. Below, pilgrims bathe in the sacred hot springs of Brahmakund, and traces of the Cyclopean Wall, built of huge undressed stones, still run across the hills. Nalanda's ruins are about 16 km to the north.

overview.text:
Nalanda was one of the great centres of learning of the ancient world. The university was founded in the 5th century CE and flourished for about 700 years, teaching Buddhist scripture, philosophy, logic, grammar, astronomy and medicine to students from across Asia; the Chinese travellers Xuanzang and Yijing left detailed accounts. Its end came with the invasion of Bakhtiyar Khilji around 1200 CE.

Today its 23-hectare archaeological site — a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2016 — reveals temples, stupas and rows of monastery blocks with stucco and stone decoration. The ASI's Nalanda Museum, founded in 1917, displays about 350 finds from the excavations. In 2024–25 the site received 88,151 foreign visitors. It lies about 16 km north of Rajgir.

items.title: Rules
items.body: Keep silent and don't climb on the ruins. Professional filming equipment needs ASI permission.

items.title: Tickets
items.body: Check current fees on the Archaeological Survey of India's official site.
Start with the museum, then walk the site with a guide.
Allow 2–3 hours; there is little shade.
